# AI Hub onboarding checklist

Work through this once. It takes about five minutes.

## 1. Confirm your access
- Sign in to the hub with your MUFG account.
- Check your profile shows the right job title and department. Your persona is derived from these, and it drives what the hub recommends.

## 2. Find an agent
- Describe what you need in the marketplace search, in plain language.
- Read the **why this matched** line before opening an agent.

## 3. Read the status before you rely on anything
| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Production | Approved for day-to-day use |
| Pilot / Beta | Limited group, expect changes |
| In development | Not for business use |

## 4. Know the access model
Open agents need no request. Request and Restricted agents route through the access portal or the owning team.

## 5. Know who to ask
Every agent page lists its owning team and a **Collaborate with the owner** action. Use it before raising a ticket.

# KYC document checklist

Use alongside the CIP Agent. The agent produces the completeness report; this is what it is checking against.

## Identity — one required
- Passport, in date
- National ID card, in date
- Driving licence, in date, photocard only

## Address — one required, issued in the last 3 months
- Utility bill, not mobile phone
- Bank or credit card statement
- Council tax or government correspondence

## Entities — additional
- Certificate of incorporation
- Register of beneficial owners
- Board resolution or equivalent authority

## Common failures
1. Address document older than three months.
2. Name on the address document does not match the application exactly.
3. Photocard licence supplied without the paper counterpart where required.
4. Scans that crop the machine-readable zone.

Anything the agent marks low confidence needs a human read before sign-off.

items.body:
# Screening dispositions cheat sheet

## The four dispositions
| Disposition | Use when | Evidence you must record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| True match | Identifiers align | The matching fields and the list entry |
| False positive | Name similarity only | Which identifiers differ |
| Insufficient information | Cannot resolve either way | What you looked for and could not find |
| Escalate | Possible true match, high risk | Everything above plus your reasoning |

## Rules
- The agent never clears a true hit. It explains and ranks; a person dispositions.
- Every disposition writes to the case audit trail before the case can close.
- Record the list refresh date shown on the result. Auditors ask for it.

## What good evidence looks like
Not "name differs". Instead: "Date of birth differs by 11 years; nationality differs; no address overlap. Screened against OFAC SDN refreshed 2026-09-07."

items.description: How to record a disposition on a screening hit so it survives audit.

# Prompt patterns for analysts

## 1. Give the context, not just the question
Weak: *Is this allowed?*
Better: *Customer in arrears asked to pause payments for 3 months. Is a payment holiday allowed under the collections policy, and what approval does it need?*

## 2. State the output you want
Weak: *Summarise this case.*
Better: *Summarise this case in five bullets: what happened, what is unusual, what has been checked, what is missing, recommended next step.*

## 3. Set the boundary
*Answer only from the approved policy library. If it is not covered, say so rather than inferring.*

## 4. Give one example
Show the shape you want once. Agents match the pattern far more reliably than they follow an abstract description.

## Anti-patterns
- Asking two unrelated questions in one prompt.
- Pasting a whole case file with no question.
- Asking for a decision the agent is not permitted to make.

# Human in the loop for customer communications

## The rule
No agent at MUFG sends a message to a customer. Agents draft; a person approves and sends. This is a conduct requirement, not a technical limitation.

## Where the line sits
| Agent may | A person must |
| --- | --- |
| Draft the message | Approve before sending |
| Choose a channel and tone | Confirm the choice fits the customer |
| Check against conduct rules | Judge vulnerability indicators |
| Schedule for approval | Release the send |

## Evidencing the approval
The approval record must capture who approved, when, and what they saw. If the draft changed after approval, it needs re-approval.

## Vulnerability
Any vulnerability indicator on the account blocks automated drafting and routes to a specialist. Do not work around this by drafting on another account.

## Why this matters
Conduct findings turn on whether a person exercised judgement. "The system generated it" is not a defence.

items.body:
# Grounding agents on policy documents

## Three rules that keep a grounded agent trustworthy

### 1. Index only approved, versioned documents
If a document is not approved, it is not in the index. Draft policy is the most common cause of a confidently wrong answer.

### 2. No citation, no answer
An answer that cannot point at the section it came from is not returned. This is enforced in the response path, not left to the prompt.

### 3. Declining is a correct outcome
When retrieval confidence is low the agent says the question is outside the library. Measure this rate; a sudden drop usually means the index broke, not that the agent improved.

## Refresh
Policy updates appear in answers within one hour of publication. Re-index on publish, not on a nightly schedule, or you will answer from withdrawn policy.

## What to test before release
- A question the library covers. Expect a cited answer.
- A question it does not cover. Expect a refusal.
- A question about withdrawn policy. Expect the current version, not the old one.

items.body:
# Document agent pattern reference

The pattern behind the CIP Agent and the Contract Analyzer.

## Flow

```text
Documents submitted
    ↓
Ingestion: virus scan, format normalisation, OCR when needed
    ↓
Extraction: model reads each page into a typed schema
    ↓
Validation: fields checked against the record and business rules
    ↓
Report: completeness and consistency findings with evidence
    ↓
Human review and sign-off
```

## Design principles
- Keep documents in the vault; pass references, not copies.
- Every extracted field carries a confidence score. Low confidence is surfaced, never hidden.
- The report, not raw model output, is the contract with downstream systems.

## What to build first
The typed schema. Everything else follows from it, and it is what makes the output testable.

The full architecture page for a live agent is linked from the marketplace.

# Agent metadata standard

Every agent registered in the hub publishes the same metadata. This is what makes search, curation and the agent page work.

## Groups
| Group | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| Identity | id, name, tagline, version |
| Business | description, problem solved, domains, use cases, personas |
| Capabilities | capabilities, services, example tasks, tags, category |
| Technical | platform, tools and services, models, architecture pattern |
| Governance | owner, status, access |
| Resources | documentation, architecture |
| Lifecycle | created, updated |

## The three that matter most
1. **Use cases** in plain language. Search matches on these more than anything else.
2. **Personas.** Curation cannot rank your agent without them.
3. **Access.** If a user cannot tell how to get in, the listing has failed.

## Submitting
Send the template filled in, or the simple flat format. The hub normalises both.

# Responsible AI certification

Four modules and a short assessment. Required before you can be named the owner or approver of an agent.

## Modules
1. **Principles** — fairness, transparency, accountability, safety.
2. **Model risk at MUFG** — risk tiers, what each tier requires, who signs off.
3. **Human in the loop** — where judgement must sit with a person.
4. **Monitoring** — what to watch after release and when to pull an agent.

## Assessment
Twenty questions. You need 80% to pass. You may retake it.

## Time
About ninety minutes end to end. It does not have to be one sitting.


This is illustrative catalog content. The enterprise source and its owner must be confirmed before this resource is published for employees.

# Writing a good AI use case request

Intake assesses on value, feasibility and risk. Give reviewers those three things and your request moves quickly.

## Structure
1. **The task today.** Who does it, how often, how long it takes.
2. **The problem.** What goes wrong or what it costs.
3. **What good looks like.** How you would know it worked.
4. **The data.** What the agent would need to read, and where it lives.
5. **The decision.** What stays with a person.

## Worked example — weak
*We want AI for onboarding.*

## Worked example — strong
*Onboarding analysts spend roughly the first 20 minutes of every case checking whether the document pack is complete, about 60 cases a week. An agent that reads the pack and lists what is missing would let them start at judgement. It would read documents from the vault and the application record. The KYC decision stays with the analyst.*

The second one can be assessed. The first cannot.

items.description: How to describe a use case so intake can assess it quickly, with two worked examples.

# Conduct rules for collections outreach

## Before any message goes out
- Contact frequency is within limits for the arrears stage.
- The channel matches the customer's stated preference where one exists.
- No vulnerability indicator is open on the account.
- Any payment arrangement referenced is one the customer actually has.

## Tone
Plain language. State the amount, the date and the options. Do not imply consequences that are not authorised at this stage.

## What the agent checks and what it cannot
| Agent checks | Person judges |
| --- | --- |
| Frequency limits | Whether contact is appropriate now |
| Template approval | Whether the tone fits this customer |
| Referenced amounts | Vulnerability signals not yet recorded |

## If in doubt
Route to a specialist. An unnecessary escalation costs minutes; a conduct breach costs far more.
